summary: The three passages are long (918-947 words) and well written, and Passage 3 on risk is genuinely IELTS-hard. But the twelve completion questions in Passages 1 and 2 copy the passage almost word for word, and the people-matching task has no extra name, so a student can score well by word-spotting. Two question groups were out of passage order and have been reordered; the paper had only 4 paraphrase pairs and now has 33.
strengths: Passage 3 ('Why we misjudge risk') is a demanding argumentative text at C1 level, with well-built MCQs whose keys paraphrase the passage (Q27 'ignorance alone' / 'a simple lack of knowledge').
Passage 2 matching-information items need real paraphrase recognition (retrofitting / buildings that already exist; benefits shared / fall to different people).
T/F/NG keys are sound: FALSE items are contradicted (curiosity at the fair, the clothing trade would not touch it, the name escaped its owner) and NOT GIVEN items are absent.

issues.problem: Y/N/NG 31-36 out of passage order: Q35 (news reporting, paragraph 2) came last, and Q36 (education, paragraph 7) came after Q34 (researchers), whose sentence follows it.
issues.change: Reordered to passage order: Q31 news organisations (NG), Q32 qualities worth caring about (YES), Q33 more accurate statistics (NO), Q34 frequency out of a hundred (YES), Q35 removed by education (NO), Q36 researchers protected (NO).

issues.problem: Sentence-completion MCQs out of order: Q37 (involuntary risk, paragraph 3) came before Q38 (heart disease, paragraph 2).
issues.change: Swapped: Q37 = heart-disease deaths underestimated, Q38 = hazard feels more threatening.

issues.problem: Broken English and a verbatim copy: 'Planted roofs are met at the lowest possible standard when cities require them without funding them.'
issues.change: Prompt now 'When cities make planted roofs compulsory without paying for them, builders do only the minimum required.' (key unchanged: Marek Dolinski).

issues.problem: Q19 prompt began 'Complete the summary.' although Questions 19-23 are separate sentences, not a summary.
issues.change: Removed the stray instruction from the prompt.

issues.problem: Pair text side 'defending his patents' is not in the passage ('defending his sewing-machine patents').
issues.change: Pair now ['busy defending his sewing-machine patents', 'concentrate on legal disputes']; 29 more pairs added.

issues.problem: Completion items 2, 5, 7, 20, 22 and 23 repeat the passage's exact phrase (joined by a cord; hollow on one face and a ... on the other; rubber overshoe; bare bitumen; patches of bare gravel). This is the main reason the paper is easier than IELTS.
issues.change: Paraphrase the stems, e.g. Q5 'one side of each tooth is hollow and the other has a ______'; Q23 'roofs that suit insects best include areas of uncovered ______'.

issues.problem: Matching people (24-26) offers exactly three names for three statements, so the last answer is free; IELTS always gives more options than questions or allows reuse.
issues.change: Add one or two extra names (e.g. the Basel or Toronto planners mentioned in paragraph A could be named) or add a fourth statement.

issues.problem: Explanations in Passages 1-2 mostly restate the evidence sentence without saying what makes the answer right or which distractor to avoid.
issues.change: Expand explanations in the style of pset1-5 (name the paraphrase and the trap).
